cohort: The participants were a cohort of children, 865 of whom were prenatally exposed to preeclampsia and 22,898 were unexposed.
finding: Prenatal exposure to preeclampsia is associated with accelerated height gain in early childhood, with exposed children growing an average of 1.6 cm more than unexposed children from birth to five years after adjustments.
birth_weight: The study notes preeclampsia is associated with low birth weight and small-for-gestational-age (SGA) births, and adjustments were made for SGA status.
gest_age: The study notes preeclampsia is associated with preterm births, and adjustments were made for gestational age at birth, finding the association with height gain was partly related to shorter gestational age at birth.
